CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for evaluation of anxiety management, persistent fatigue, sleep quality, headache intensity, and medication adjustment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, expressing slight improvement in his overall anxiety levels and sleep quality since the last visit. He reports that increasing the dose of Amitriptyline to 25 mg nightly has contributed positively to his sleep, with fewer awakenings during the night. He describes his sleep as "more restful," although he still experiences difficulty waking up in the morning. Daytime fatigue persists, but he feels somewhat more alert, attributing this to the combined effect of Amitriptyline and Modafinil.
Despite these improvements, Mr. Smith continues to face significant anxiety, particularly related to his workload and performance pressures. He has been utilizing coping strategies discussed in the previous appointment, which have proven helpful, yet he still finds himself overwhelmed at times.
Regarding his tension-type headaches, Mr. Smith reports that while the frequency remains stable at four episodes per week, the intensity has shown minimal improvement. He describes the headaches as "annoying" rather than debilitating, but they still disrupt his work. He has been alternating between Ibuprofen and Acetaminophen for relief, which has provided some benefit, but he expresses a desire for a more effective long-term solution.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General: Persistent fatigue; no significant weight changes noted. Cardiovascular: Intermittent palpitations stable; denies chest pain or edema. Respiratory: No shortness of breath; CPAP compliance noted; no cough or wheezing. Gastrointestinal: Mild nausea persists; occasional bloating; no vomiting or changes in bowel habits. Neurological: Stable headache frequency with slight reduction in intensity; no photophobia or phonophobia noted.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Mild obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed on sleep study. - Tension-type headaches.
FAMILY HISTORY
- Father: Coronary artery disease, underwent CABG at age 60. - Mother: Hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
- Lives alone in , . Works as a teacher. No tobacco use; social alcohol consumption. No illicit drug use.
MEDICATIONS
- Atorvastatin 10 mg daily. - Magnesium supplement 400 mg daily. - Melatonin 5 mg nightly. - Escitalopram 30 mg daily. - Amitriptyline 25 mg nightly. - Modafinil 100 mg daily. - CPAP machine for sleep apnea.
ALLERGIES
- No known drug allergies.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
VITALS: T 98.4F, HR 80 bpm, BP 118/74 mmHg, RR 16 breaths/min, O2 sat 96% on room air.
General: Well-nourished, alert, appears fatigued but in no acute distress. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. No peripheral edema. Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally; CPAP device noted, no wheezing or crackles. Gastrointestinal: Soft, non-tender abdomen; no epigastric tenderness. Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no focal deficits. Mild tenderness noted on palpation of the bilateral temporalis region.
LABORATORY DATA
Lipid Panel (obtained at last visit): Total Cholesterol 158 mg/dL, LDL 78 mg/dL, HDL 64 mg/dL, Triglycerides 80 mg/dL CBC: Normal BMP: Normal TSH: Normal
RADIOLOGICAL STUDIES
- No new studies indicated at this visit.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Persistent fatigue and anxiety with ongoing sleep disturbances. - Mr. Smith reports slight improvement in both anxiety and sleep quality. We will continue the current regimen of Melatonin 5 mg nightly and Escitalopram 30 mg daily. Given the positive response to Amitriptyline, we will maintain the current dosage of 25 mg nightly. We will discuss the potential addition of cognitive-behavioral therapy to further address anxiety symptoms. Schedule a follow-up in 4 weeks to monitor progress.
2. Stable frequency but minimal improvement in intensity of tension-type headaches. - The patient reports no significant change in headache intensity. We will continue with Amitriptyline at the current dosage and consider a referral to a neurologist for further evaluation and management if symptoms do not improve. Follow-up in 4 weeks to reassess headache frequency and severity.
3. Lipid management. - Continue Atorvastatin 10 mg daily as lipid levels remain stable. Reassess lipid panel in 3 months to evaluate ongoing effectiveness.
4. Follow-up. - Schedule follow-up appointment in 4 weeks to reassess anxiety symptoms, sleep quality, headache frequency, and overall well-being. Discuss potential referrals for cognitive-behavioral therapy if anxiety symptoms persist or worsen.
